requirements.statement: Extend the package-owned AIDLC bundle resolver with offline, bounded-lock, content-addressed project projection that atomically creates or reuses one immutable verified pack, writes separate projection and future-run selector receipts, preserves idempotence, fails closed without mutating unsafe or conflicting state, and supports explicit bounded stale-staging recovery.

path_bindings.ownership_evidence: The completed Phase 2A.1 run established this package-owned resolver as the provider, integrity, trust, and receipt owner; Phase 2A.2 extends that same boundary with project projection.

proof_bindings.asserted_behavior: Pack identity, safe target validation, bounded lock acquisition, atomic staging, selector validation, idempotent reuse, and recovery targeting behave deterministically against controlled filesystem fixtures.

Projection and selector receipts are separate closed versioned contracts that bind the ready resolver receipt, exact copied inventory, immutable pack identity, trust posture, project path, and stable fingerprints.

A first offline provision creates one verified pack, repeat and racing calls reuse it without churn, unsafe or conflicting state remains untouched, and only explicit bounded recovery removes a validated stale staging directory.

positive: A ready Phase 2A.1 receipt projects into one immutable content-addressed pack through one bounded cross-platform lock and exact-byte atomic transaction.
Projection and future-run selector receipts remain separate, closed, fingerprinted contracts.
Repeat and concurrent calls are idempotent, while explicit bounded recovery owns only validated managed staging state.
negative: Provisioning never contacts the network, executes pack content, mutates source bytes, overwrites occupied state, silently retargets a selector, or cleans pre-existing staging state during an ordinary call.
This slice does not implement active-run binding, Requirements lookup, public Full routing, host projection, schema files, package registration, or documentation.
